title: Hear What God the Lord Hath Spoken
description: Hear What God the Lord Hath Spoken in Tonic Solfa to LUX EOI, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 65, “The future peace and glory of the church. Isa 60:15-20”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7.8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to LUX EOI; any other Eights and Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hear what God the Lord hath spo-ken, O my peo-ple, faint and few; Com-fort-less, a-fflic-ted, bro-ken, Fair a-bodes I build for you: Themes of heart felt tri-bu-la-tion Shall no more per-plex your ways; You shall name your walls, Sal-va-tion, And your gates shall all be praise.

lines: Hear what God the Lord hath spoken,
O my people, faint and few;
Comfortless, afflicted, broken,
Fair abodes I build for you:
Themes of heart-felt tribulation
Shall no more perplex your ways;
You shall name your walls, Salvation,
And your gates shall all be praise.
There, like streams that feed the garden,
Pleasures, without end, shall flow;
For the Lord, your faith rewarding,
All his bounty shall bestow:
Still in undisturbed possession,
Peace and righteousness shall reign;
Never shall you feel oppression,
Hear the voice of war again.
Ye no more your suns descending,
Waning moons no more shall see,
But your griefs, for ever ending,
Find eternal noon in me:
God shall rise, and shining o'er you,
Change to day the gloom of night;
He, the Lord, shall be your glory,
God your everlasting light.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to LUX EOI by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
